From the 1960s millions of Moroccans moved abroad to work, above all to France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain and Italy. They are one of the largest migrant groups in Europe.

Labour treaties signed in the 1960s with France, West Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands invited workers for mines, factories and farms. Many came from the poor Rif mountains of the north. When the recruiting stopped in the 1970s, families joined them and they stayed. Later waves went to Spain and Italy, some crossing the strait in small boats.

Money sent home is one of Morocco's largest sources of foreign currency. Moroccan Europeans include politicians, footballers and writers. See also Morocco, France and Spain.
sum: From the 1960s millions of Moroccans moved abroad to work, above all to France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain and Italy. They are one of the largest migrant groups in Europe.
